review_type: Independent adversarial source, parity, and UI/UX review of mobile document roots and directory navigation, multi-state parameter row styling, and hover metadata tooltips
verdict: REJECTED for exact-clone parity (Score: 6.0/10). Critical UI/UX and cross-platform navigation capabilities verified: FilePicker supports mobile document roots (Android /sdcard/Download, /sdcard/Documents, /storage/emulated/0, iOS Documents) and nested subdirectory navigation with '📁 .. (Up)' directory traversal; ParamEditor parameter grid delivers complete multi-state visual indicators matching C# ConfigRawParams (green for staged edits, yellow for writes pending ACK, red for failed writes, and reverted background for confirmed writes); right-click context menus support 'Set to default' and 'Revert changes'; and rich multi-line documentation tooltips display on hover with parameter names, descriptions, ranges, units, defaults, options, bitmasks, and live autopilot state badges. All 203 workspace tests pass cleanly with zero warnings. However, modern Android Scoped Storage (API 30+) and iOS sandboxing continue to restrict posix filesystem access without OS-level SAF/UIDocumentPicker dialogs, and parameter write post-completion reboot prompting remains unhandled.

findings.subsystem: Mobile Scoped Storage & Native SAF File Picker Bridge
evidence: document_roots() in crates/mp-app/src/platform.rs queries posix filesystem paths (/sdcard/Download, /storage/emulated/0).

On Android 11+ (API level 30+), Scoped Storage enforces SELinux isolation where direct posix access to /storage/emulated/0 is blocked for non-manager apps without using the Storage Access Framework (SAF / Intent.ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT). Similarly, iOS external file access requires UIDocumentPickerViewController to issue security-scoped resource bookmarks.
findings.impact: On modern Android and iOS devices, operators cannot access files in shared device storage or third-party cloud drives without OS SAF/DocumentPicker delegation.
findings.required_fix: Implement JNI intent dispatch for Android SAF (ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT / ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT) and Objective-C/Swift UIDocumentPickerViewController bindings on iOS.

findings.subsystem: Parameter reboot required detection and post-write prompt
evidence: In C# ConfigRawParams.cs (BUT_writePIDS_Click lines 324-328), parameter writes check ParameterMetaDataRepository.GetParameterRebootRequired(value). If any modified parameter requires reboot, reboot is flagged, and the user is prompted to reboot the autopilot after writing.
In Rust ParamEditor::write_confirm_window, written parameters are sent over the link, but reboot requirement metadata is not checked, and no post-write reboot prompt is displayed.
findings.impact: Operators modifying parameters that require flight controller reboot (e.g. communication baud rates, sensor configurations) may fly with unapplied parameters unaware that a reboot is necessary.
findings.required_fix: Inspect param_meta::get(fw, name).reboot_required during write_confirm_window execution, track reboot requirement, and prompt the operator to reboot the autopilot upon completion.

evidence: In C# ConfigRawParams.cs, searching for a parameter or typing in the search box dynamically expands the corresponding category node in the left-hand TreeView and scrolls the selected node into view.
In Rust ParamEditor, entering text in self.search filters the parameter table rows, but does not auto-select or expand the matching group in the category tree.
findings.impact: Operators using the search bar must manually find and navigate the corresponding tree category.
findings.required_fix: When self.search matches a single parameter group, automatically expand and highlight that group in treeView1.
